description: Build a complete house from scratch using homeowner-style natural language requests
note: Prompts use everyday language — no block types, no connector names, no technical details. The agent must figure out the right approach.

steps.utterance: We're setting up a new smart home. We have these rooms: living room, bedroom, kitchen, bathroom, hallway, garden, and garage. Can you set it up?
We need weather data — temperature, sunshine, wind, rain, humidity, and how bright it is outside.
Every room needs smart lights. The garden light should be called Gartenbeleuchtung and the garage one Garagenlicht.
Add blinds to all rooms except the garden and garage — two per room. Also add a motorized projection screen in the living room.
The living room needs a thermostat and air conditioning. Add room temperature sensors for the living room and bedroom.
We need a motion sensor in the hallway and one in the garden. Also a doorbell, a front door sensor, and a garage door sensor.

The bathroom needs a fan and a radiator we can control. The garden needs an irrigation valve, a pool pump, and a soil moisture sensor. Add a CO2 sensor for the living room and a pool temperature sensor.
We need two general purpose switches and a manual irrigation button.
When someone walks through the hallway, turn on the light. The front door opening should also trigger the hallway light for about a minute and a half.
The bathroom gets really steamy after showers. Can you make the fan turn on automatically and keep running for a few minutes after?
At night, the hallway and bathroom lights should be much dimmer — maybe 20% — so they don't wake anyone up.
Connect the room temperature sensor to the living room thermostat so it knows the current temperature.
When it gets really windy, the blinds should go up everywhere for protection. Same when it rains — close them.
On hot sunny days, close the living room and bedroom blinds automatically to keep the house cool.
The pool pump should run when the water gets cold, but not when it's freezing outside — we don't want frozen pipes.
The garden should water itself when the soil is dry, but not when it's raining. The manual button should still work too.
When someone moves in the garden at night, turn on the light. Also, the garage light should stay on for five minutes after the door opens.
The second switch should open and close the garage door.
When the doorbell rings, buzz the door open for 3 seconds and turn on the hallway light so they can see.
If the garage door opens at night, turn on the garden light for a few minutes as well — I want to see who's there.
Movie night: when I press switch 2, the projection screen should come down, living room lights go to 10%, and the AC turns on.
Good night mode on switch 1: turn off all lights, close the bedroom blinds, and if someone walks through the hallway, only 5% light.
Water the garden every morning from 6 to 6:30. And turn on the garden lights automatically in the evening, say from 8pm to midnight.
Don't start the AC unless it's been hot for at least 10 minutes — I don't want it cycling on and off all day.
